Outcome_variable.evidence_source:
[/page/5/Text/9] In Study 1, we examined the relationship between extraversion, social experiences, and satisfaction using a 4-year study of college men. The results indicate that while extraversion predicts future college satisfaction and social
[/page/5/Text/10] experiences throughout college, social experiences do not help explain the association between extraversion and college satisfaction. More extraverted students were more satisfied with college and had more positive social experiences, but they were not more satisfied with college because they had more positive peer experiences.
[/page/5/Text/11] Study 1 did have some limitations. [...] Additionally, there is not a measure of happiness or positive affect that would allow for a test of whether these results are unique to college satisfaction or are shared by the affective component of subjective well-being.
